scores.evidence: Phase 2 "Finalize help-center ingestion" and Phase 3 "Session management... memory" after retrieval; but V0 skeleton already uses retrieval before ETL/chunking proven
scores.rationale: Mostly substrate-upward (skeleton, defenses, retrieval, orchestration, feedback), but ETL/chunking are finalized after the skeleton already uses retrieval, and observability/security hardening sits in Phase 3.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 ... POST /api/v1/chat ... Deployed via Docker container ... CI/CD pipeline: commit → build image → ... deploy
scores.rationale: A real end-to-end path across API, retrieval, vector store, embedding, LLM and logging with deploy and rollback is Phase 0, although it is only staging and internal.

scores.evidence: Hosted API vs self-host model | R3 ... Default: Hosted API ... Flip condition: Cost per token exceeds ASSUMPTION consistently, or latency SLA violated
scores.rationale: The plan has a table of irreversible decisions with reversibility class, default, validation and flip condition, and it labels assumptions and unknowns.

scores.evidence: Tasks (in blast-radius order): 1. Input validation and injection filter (wide impact: affects every request).
scores.rationale: Phase 1 explicitly orders tasks by blast radius, and the phases themselves put wide-impact defenses before leaf capabilities.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 | Injection payload logged; API request/response sanitized (PII redaction stub); cost cap enforced (hard 1k token limit)
scores.rationale: The cross-cutting table gives concrete security treatment for every phase 0–4, starting at Phase 0, although Phase 0 has no auth.

scores.evidence: Logs: Every request/response pair logged as JSON with trace ID, latency (ms), tokens, cost, model name, and any error.
scores.rationale: Observability begins in Phase 0 with structured logs and baseline metrics, and it continues with concrete content in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Code in Git (commit hash in every deployment); model name and embedding model pinned (no auto-upgrade); prompt template committed
scores.rationale: Each phase has concrete reproducibility measures: pinned models, versioned indexes, CI test suites, and git-tagged config and prompts.

scores.evidence: Timeout on every external call (retrieval, LLM, embedding): 10 s hard stop; graceful degradation returns "temporarily unavailable"
scores.rationale: Resilience content appears in every phase: timeouts in Phase 0, circuit breaker in Phase 1, ETL retries and index rollback in Phase 2, fallbacks in Phase 3, flag-based rollback in Phase 4.

scores.evidence: Human-in-the-loop gating | ... | Phase 2 ... Retrieval | Phase 1 (skeleton), Phase 2 (tuning)
scores.rationale: Defenses and budgets come first in Phase 1 and the order of retrieval, model access, memory, orchestration and feedback is right, but human-in-the-loop lands in Phase 2 after the skeleton, and model access and retrieval are built in Phase 0 before the defenses.

scores.evidence: Multi-model routing by difficulty/cost: Deferred until Phase 4 canary shows that 10% of queries could be handled by a cheaper model... Flip: cost per query exceeds budget by > 20%
scores.rationale: The plan lists six deferred items, each with a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: This is a strong, thorough plan with a real Phase 0 skeleton, gated decisions and threaded cross-cutting concerns. Its main weaknesses are that retrieval and model access run in Phase 0 before the defenses and human-in-the-loop are in place, and that some ordering is loose (ETL and observability hardening come late).
